To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) belief in traditional roles in marriage was associated with less marital satisfaction and lower empathic listening, but (b) only when the belief was not coupled with belief in the equal sharing of such traditional roles.
the belief in equality in a marriage was positively correlated with empathic listening and marital satisfaction, and that empathic listening mediated this relationship.
the belief that one should not expect equality in one’s marital roles is associated with lower marital satisfaction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between traditional marital expectations and relationship satisfaction, and how this relationship is mediated by listening styles.

how the cultural beliefs and expectations about the role of women and men in marriage affect the ways in which Indo-Pakistanis listen to their spouse and how this in turn affects their marital satisfaction.
the relationship satisfaction among South Asian Canadians and the role of ‘complementary-equality’ and listening to understand.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a greater adherence to traditional expectations of marriage was associated with lower levels of marital satisfaction and lower levels of listening styles in the relationship.

the findings of this study suggest that a more traditional view of marital relationships, specifically the belief that men and women have complementary roles in the relationship, may be related to lower levels of interpersonal communication in one’s marriage.

the more a person adheres to the traditional beliefs about marriage, the less likely he or she would be able to understand the partner’s point of view and the more likely they would be to be dissatisfied in their marriage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the more one adheres to traditional marital expectations, the lower one’s marital satisfaction and interpersonal listening.
adherence to traditional marital roles in ones relationship is associated with lower levels of listening and marital satisfaction, but only if such roles are undertaken with a belief in inequality.

the degree to which one believes in upholding equality, in undertaking the traditional roles of husband and wife, is associated with greater levels of interpersonal listening in ones relationship and higher levels of marital satisfaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Indo-Pakistani women and men can be more satisfied in their marriages by being more egalitarian, and by listening more to each other.
it is important to listen to your partner and to listen to understand.

it is not necessarily the adherence to traditional marital values that is problematic for marital satisfaction among Indo-Pakistanis, but the degree to which they adhere to the notion of equality in undertaking traditional roles.
